findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. A skipped required check is a failure in `src/forge/checks.py:124-137`, but `worker._failing` in `src/forge/worker.py:459-464` includes only checks with bucket `fail`. When that skipped check stops close, this condition leaves `what` empty and re-raises close's `forge work <item>` instruction. The queue therefore gives the wrong next step instead of the promised `forge land <item>` fix rounds. The new tests do not exercise this check outcome.
findings.title: Not done: failing required skipped checks route to forge land

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Test. The timed assertion checks only that `apple` enters review last. It still passes if `banana` enters before the older `cherry`, so the required oldest-first close-start order is unproved. The test's parent `Starting` lines show launch order, but do not establish when the children enter close.
findings.title: Not done: test_1 proves the closes start oldest first

stop.reason: Coordinator (Harm 1-2, reversible; first stop in land.py): one round with a structural move: the queue reads each change's check status from the same Forge function the board and next use (no own mapping), and the two tests get ordered timestamps at close entry plus the due-default and worker-stuck stop cases. Further edge findings here become follow-ups.
